writeup: TIC 403069594 is a candidate eclipsing binary star system with an orbital period of 1.5145 days. Observations from TESS photometry show a primary eclipse causing the system to dim by 4.94%, while no secondary eclipse was detected. The eclipse signal achieved a high statistical significance with a box-least-squares detection signal-to-noise ratio of 411.7. Pixel-level image analysis using difference imaging confirmed the signal with a peak signal-to-noise of 39.8, though the centroid offset measured 4.3 arcsec from the target location. The candidate does not appear in any of six checked variable-star catalogs, making it a novel candidate. The machine-learning screening model assigned it a score of 0.52 on a scale where higher values indicate greater confidence in the target's validity.
